_m4_consent_registry._selector_collision_WARNING: recordVerificationZK(uint256[2],uint256[2][2],uint256[2],uint256[7]) = 0xdd080593, which is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the RETIRED Level-A 4-arg selector (see _verification_registry_redeploy) - same ABI shape, COMPLETELY different pub semantics (Level-A pub[3]=subject/pub[4]=nullifier/pub[6]=R vs Level-B pub[3]=nullifier/pub[4]=R/pub[6]=deadline). A stale pre-PR#7 client aimed at this registry would DISPATCH rather than bounce, but fails closed twice (R!=profileRoot, then a Level-A proof cannot verify against the consent VK). Conversely a Level-B client aimed at the LIVE Level-A registry 0x4E2f0996 (which only dispatches the 6-arg 0x423a45b6) gets the bare `execution reverted, data: 0x` - the exact confusing symptom from data/dogtag-zkfail-z9. Check the ADDRESS first when debugging either.

m5_requirements.profileRoot: M5 MUST set profileRoot(dogTagId) = R, the per-tag Merkle root of the M1-engine tree (3 reserved owner leaves + attribute leaves). The SBT already stores profileRoot as bytes32 - NO SBT change is needed for M4. The registry asserts R == profileRoot(dogTagId); this is the ONLY place dogTagId <-> R is bound (the circuit deliberately does not).
m5_requirements.issue_the_root: M5 MUST ALSO issue(R) the per-tag root into a DogTagIssuer clone, not only setProfileRoot. The registry keeps the Level-A revocation path (resolve rootIssuer[R] -> clone, require isValid(R)), so a root that is only set as profileRoot and never issued reverts 'unknown root' on EVERY verify. This preserves revocation under Level-B: revoke(R) stops the tag verifying.
m5_requirements.custodial_mint: D1: mint to a neutral custodian, never the owner. The registry reads profileRoot for the binding and ownerOf for token EXISTENCE only (value DISCARDED, never compared), so a custodial ownerOf is correct and inert - ConsentRegistry.t.sol proves verification passes with ownerOf == custodian. The ownerOf call is NOT an owner-identity check: it exists because DogTagSBT.burn (GDPR-erasure) does not clear profileRoot[id], so R == profileRoot still passes for an erased tag, and OZ ownerOf (_requireOwned) reverting on a burned token is what fails erasure closed - see test_burned_tag_cannot_verify.
m5_requirements.profileRoot_mutability_RESOLVED_IN_M5: M5 resolves the mutable-root gap structurally with DogTagSBTConsent: profileRoot is set only by mintCustodial and there is no setProfileRoot function. The canonical M5 registry is constructed against that SBT. This M4 registry remains unsafe for real Level-B credentials because its immutable sbt pointer cannot be changed.

m7_cutover._note: TWO canonical Level-B addresses must move TOGETHER in M7, not one: (1) VerificationRegistry 0x4E2f0996... -> VerificationRegistryConsent 0xb9B313C17fD8725Bb50A7f41121ac4Cf5F4fec87, AND (2) DogTagSBT 0x1FB8986573Ac36d532cF7d5a5352202B094D4233 -> DogTagSBTConsent 0x96Cba4580D79bc9b8e51Fc1B3a044A29592AfFFc. Repoint ONLY in M7, when the apps prove against the M3 consent VK and the Level-B custodial issuance path is ready. The on-chain M5 prerequisite is deployed, but repointing now would break the live flow because today's clients still send Level-A proofs. Never point a consumer at the superseded M4 registry 0x53F988Ae.... Repointing only ONE of the two addresses, or only some consumers, is exactly the split-brain recorded in _verification_registry_redeploy - the swap is not done until BOTH keys move everywhere below.

m7_cutover.docs_normative_levelA_semantics: These carry the NORMATIVE Level-A verify semantics (the subject-bearing Verified event, the keyOf/ownerOf==subject checks, the pub=[dogTagId,purpose,relayer,subject,nullifier,keyHash,R] vector, the ECDSA path) and go STALE the moment Level-B is the live path - they are deliberately untouched by M4 (Level-A is still live and they describe it accurately), but M7 MUST revise them, not just swap addresses: docs/architecture.md (§4.1 contract set + §4.7 VerificationRegistry normative body), docs/implementation.md (§2.6 'Three new contracts' + the §11.8 normative bodies), docs/ROLE_APPS.md (the contract list + the verifier-role descriptions).
m7_cutover.docs_dpia: docs/DPIA.md is a self-declared LIVING document that 'MUST be refreshed whenever the on-chain data model, the verification subsystem, or the erasure flow change'. Level-B changes all three: the Verified linkage row (line ~36) is scored on `subject`+dogTagId+relayer and its mitigation is 'fresh per-pet subject' - under Level-B there IS no subject, so the row must be RE-SCORED, not just edited. The re-scoring itself needs a data-protection judgement (DPO/captain) and is deliberately NOT done while Level-B is not live - crediting the live system with a privacy improvement it does not yet have is the dangerous direction to be wrong in for a regulatory artifact. M4 instead added docs/DPIA.md section 2.1, a FORWARD-LOOKING note recording the refresh as QUEUED and naming the three rows that must be re-scored (verification-event linkage, wallet<->SBT link, and the erasure-flow burn mitigation); every current Level-A risk row/rating/mitigation is untouched and still accurate. M7 MUST perform the actual re-scoring, and GDPR Art. 35 wants it done BEFORE processing starts, i.e. before the cutover - not after.

_m4_consent_registry._levelb_ecdsa_path: There is deliberately NO ECDSA recordVerification on this registry. That path asserts ownerOf(dogTagId) == subject, which under D1 (custodial mint) resolves to the custodian and can never match a real owner - it is structurally dead under Level-B, and its subject-revealing Verified event would undo the circuit's purpose. Legacy ECDSA verification keeps working, unchanged, on the Level-A registry 0x4E2f0996 for as long as Level-A tags exist. If Level-B ever needs a non-ZK fallback that is a NEW spec decision (the owner has no on-chain identity to sign as), not a port of the Level-A path.
_m4_consent_registry._supersedes_stale_deploy: This address REPLACES the first M4 deploy 0x57A2998... (kept above as VerificationRegistryConsent_preErasureGate_legacy, block 194489, runtime 6179 bytes). That instance was deployed BEFORE the review-round hardening that added the ownerOf token-existence gate, so its bytecode LACKS the erasure gate: a GDPR-burned tag would still verify there. It was never live and no consumer ever pointed at it. This redeploy (runtime 6317 bytes) carries the gate and is byte-identical to the committed source, so the recorded address and the shipped code agree - which is the point: a canonical address whose bytecode differs from source is the same landmine class as data/dogtag-zkfail-z9. Do NOT use 0x57A2998.

_m5_custodial_issuance.issuance_is_two_writes: vacc.issue(R) into a DogTagIssuer clone AND sbt.mintCustodial(dogTagId, R). Minting alone yields a tag that reverts 'unknown root' on EVERY verify, because the registry resolves the issuing clone from the root (rootIssuer[R] -> isValid(R)) to keep revoke(R) working. The spec's step list names only profileRoot, so this is the trap.
_m5_custodial_issuance.m7_handoff: M7 must explicitly grant the intended issuance actor, complete the owner-device tree flow, update Level-B proof/event consumers, and repoint every consumer on the file-by-file list at _m4_consent_registry.m7_cutover. That cutover is a TWO-ADDRESS swap and both halves must land together: VerificationRegistry 0x4E2f0996... -> VerificationRegistryConsent 0xb9B313C17fD8725Bb50A7f41121ac4Cf5F4fec87, AND DogTagSBT 0x1FB8986573Ac36d532cF7d5a5352202B094D4233 -> DogTagSBTConsent 0x96Cba4580D79bc9b8e51Fc1B3a044A29592AfFFc. The SBT half is not a config-only edit: DogTagSBTConsent replaces mint(to,id,root) with mintCustodial(id,root) and has no setProfileRoot, so the vet-api AND admin-api issuance paths are a code rework, not a config edit (see _m4_consent_registry.m7_cutover.backend_issuance_path_SBT_swap and .backend_admin_api_SBT_swap). The m4 key is DEPRECATED as an address but still owns the canonical cutover checklist - read it, do not skip it because of its status header; repointing only one address, or only some consumers, is exactly the split-brain recorded in _verification_registry_redeploy. This M5 deployment changed no consumer configuration.
_m5_custodial_issuance.profileRoot_is_write_once: DogTagSBTConsent has NO setProfileRoot at all - the root is set at mint and sealed. This structurally closes the setProfileRoot hijack that AGENTS.md flagged for M5 (R == profileRoot is the SOLE tag<->owner binding once M4 removed the ownerOf/keyOf identity checks, so a mutable root is a forgery vector). The seal also survives a burn/re-mint: mintCustodial rejects any id whose profileRoot is already set, because ERC-721 _burn leaves no tombstone and _mint only rejects a re-mint when the previous owner was non-zero, so without that guard an ISSUER holder could burn a tag and re-mint the same id under an attacker root. Consequence: a tag's tree is FROZEN at issuance and a dogTagId is single-use FOREVER (a burned/GDPR-erased id can never be re-minted) - any change means a fresh tag, exactly as D3 already mandates for recovery.

_IssuerDomainRegistry_provenance: 2026-07-28: deployed STANDALONE against the EXISTING fresh-set factory + registry via contracts/script/DeployIssuerDomainRegistry.s.sol - deliberately NOT Deploy.s.sol, which also constructs a fresh IssuerRegistry/DogTagIssuerImpl/DogTagIssuerFactory and overwrites those keys here; a new factory is unrecoverable because VerificationRegistryConsent.rootIndex is immutable, so every root issued by a new clone would resolve rootIssuer[R] == 0 and strand the issuer-whitelist pillar. deploy tx 0x44e385c28a655ab22056ea9e41390de4665fe3ef1efb69560289d6238195ac66 (block 292145), signer = deployer 0x119F8c7F6D7EC10E7376983739C6f46cF9CC3E96 (this deploy needs NO role; it only constructs). VERIFIED: deployed runtime is byte-identical to the compiled source once the 8 immutable slots are blanked (5023 bytes); factory() and issuerRegistry() (NOTE: the getter is issuerRegistry(), not registry()) return exactly those two addresses; setDomain from an unauthorized sender on the REAL TRAVEL_CLEARANCE clone reverts NotAuthorized 0xea8e4eb5, setDomain on a non-clone reverts NotAClone 0x3ce914e4, and an uppercase or single-label domain reverts BadDomain 0x9d135ed2. SCOPE: the registry is EMPTY (boundCloneCount == 0, no domain bound). This changes nothing a user sees until domains are bound - it does NOT make domain verification work. What it does is move the app's honest 'the on-chain domain claim could not be read' into a state where a claim CAN be read once one is published. Consumers wired in the same change: stacks/admin/web/.env.example (VITE_ISSUER_DOMAIN_REGISTRY_ADDR), stacks/government/.env.example (ISSUER_DOMAIN_REGISTRY_ADDR), and the two compile-time mobile bundles apps/ios/DogTag/roax.json + apps/android/app/src/main/assets/roax.json (both need an app rebuild + reinstall to take effect). scripts/demo-up.sh needed no edit - it already resolves this key from this ledger.
